summary: Built by a pulp company in the 1940s, staffed by the province until 2012 and demolished by 2015; only fields and foundations remain in Cape Chignecto park.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia's history section gives closure in 2013 and demolition in June 2015. The CBC report, carried by Yahoo, says the province decommissioned its towers in 2015 and dismantled them. The dates differ; both leave the tower gone. Wikipedia's geography section still says 'just north of the New Yarmouth fire tower' in the present tense; the history section is the dated account and is used here.

sources.title: Gap Filler Detail, 1960 letter on a forestry tower near New Yarmouth, NS (National Archives of Canada file S10-136-80/5)
'Not relics from the past': Some firefighters think N.S. should bring back fire lookout towers

notes_for_editor: The brief's 'gone' status holds. Most dated facts (1940s build, 1999 retirement, 2012 last staffing, 2013 closure, June 2015 demolition) rest on Wikipedia, which cites a 2013 CBC article and a Maritimes scanning page; the CBC 2013 page timed out, and the scanning page was not read, so those dates are not checked against their own sources. Wikipedia's geography section still uses the present tense for the tower. The 70 ft (21.3 m) height is from the 1960 letter and may not match the tower of later years. The build year is only 'the 1940s', so no build event is recorded. The brief's local_unit 'Cumberland County' is left out of the story, since Canadian towers are not given a county. Record coordinates (45.3685, -64.8468) lie about 1.6 km from the Wikipedia community point (45.3754, -64.8296); not checked against the tower site. Staffing ended in 2012 per Wikipedia, which also says the tower was staffed seasonally, so no year-round status is claimed. Access is public by way of the park; no source describes the site as closed.
